description:
# Goal

`Filament.Cell` is meant to be the transport-agnostic subscription API that lets Filament work with non-web backends (e.g. OctoPi TUI). Today it is half-built: defined as a behaviour, with one transport (`Filament.Observable.GenServer`), a public hook (`use_cell/2`), and a notify path that sends `{:cell_update, ...}` messages — but **nothing receives those messages on the web backend**. All four example apps subscribe via the older `use_observable` / `%Filament.Observable.Subscriber{}` path instead.

This epic finishes Cell, migrates everything onto it, and deletes the Subscriber model and the web-specific concerns it dragged into the supposedly-neutral observable layer (`session_token`, `via_registry`, Phoenix-LV-aware resubscribe).

# Why delete Subscriber, not Cell

The Subscriber path is mature and works, but it is web-specific by design — the `session_token` field exists to support LiveView reconnect handoff, and the resubscribe message types are LV-shaped. A TUI/CLI backend would either reinvent these concepts or implement a fake LV-shaped path; neither is acceptable. Cell is the right shape; it is just incomplete.

# Current dual-mode footprint

- `lib/filament/cell.ex` — behaviour (subscribe/2, unsubscribe/1, current/1)
- `lib/filament/observable/gen_server.ex` — implements both:
  - Cell-side: `@behaviour Filament.Cell`, `handle_call({:filament_cell_subscribe, ...}, ...)`, `handle_cell_subscribe/3`, `handle_cell_current/2`, `handle_cell_unsubscribe/1`, `notify_cell_each/2`, sends `{:cell_update, sub, projected}` (line 334).
  - Subscriber-side: `handle_call({:filament_subscribe, %Subscriber{}}, ...)`, `handle_legacy_subscribe/3`, `legacy_subscribe_handoff/5`, `legacy_subscribe_merge/5`, `handle_legacy_remove_projection/4`, `legacy_remove_projection_for/6`, sends `{:filament_observable_updates, [...]}` with backpressure and resubscribe-on-saturation.
  - Process dictionary holds both kinds of subscribers in `:__filament_subscribers__`; `notify_observers/1` fans out to both.
- `lib/filament/hooks.ex` — both hooks:
  - `use_cell/2` (lines ~372-422) → slot state `{:cell_subscribed, raw}`
  - `use_observable/1,2` (lines ~208-285) → slot state `{:subscribed, server, raw}`, uses `%Subscriber{}`, supports dynamic server swap
- `lib/filament/live_view.ex` — `handle_info` clauses for `:filament_set_state`, `:filament_observable_updates`, `:filament_observable_resubscribe`. **No `:cell_update` clause.**
- `lib/filament/live_component.ex` — same surface via `process_filament_msg/3`. **No `:cell_update` clause.**
- `lib/filament/observable.ex`, `lib/filament/observable/subscriber.ex` — Subscriber struct + GenServer.call/cast wrappers.
- Tests: `test/filament/cell_test.exs`, `test/filament/observable/cell_impl_test.exs`, `test/filament/hooks/use_cell_test.exs` exercise Cell against test pids — never through a real LV. Subscriber path has integration coverage in `test/filament/observable_test.exs`, `test/filament/observable/backpressure_test.exs`, `test/filament/reconciler_test.exs`, etc.
- Examples: cart, collaboration, inventory, todo all use `use_observable` only.

# Capability gap (Cell vs Subscriber today)

| | Subscriber | Cell |
|---|---|---|
| LV/LiveComponent receives updates | ✅ | ❌ no handler |
| Backpressure (mailbox saturation) | ✅ | ❌ unconditional `send` |
| Resubscribe-on-saturation/error | ✅ | ❌ |
| Dynamic server swap detection | ✅ slot tag carries `server` | ❌ slot tag has no identity |
| Session/reconnect handoff | ✅ via `session_token` | ❌ |
| `use_*/1` factory-fn → resolved server | ✅ `use_observable/1` | ❌ no `use_cell/1` |

# Open design questions (resolve before step 4)

**Q1. Session/reconnect handoff.** Subscriber path lets a new LV pid reclaim an existing subscription via `session_token`. Two options for Cell:
  (a) Add `claim/3` (or similar) to the Cell behaviour — every transport implements. Keeps the abstraction symmetric but forces every transport to think about handoff even if it doesn't apply (a TUI process probably doesn't reconnect).
  (b) Push handoff into the web-adapter layer — LV-side code holds the (subscriber-tuple ↔ session-token) mapping and calls `subscribe`/`unsubscribe` itself. Keeps Cell minimal but duplicates handoff logic per backend.
  Lean: (b). Cell stays small; web-specific concerns stay in web-specific code.

**Q2. Public hook naming.** Once Subscriber is gone, do we keep `use_cell` as the name, or rename it to `use_observable` (reusing the familiar name with new semantics)? Lean: rename to `use_observable`, since 'cell' is internal jargon and consumers don't care which behaviour their value comes through. The behaviour module stays `Filament.Cell`.

# Verification gates

Each child task must leave green: `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`, `mix test`, `mix credo --strict`, `mix dialyzer`. Final task additionally verifies all four example apps in Chrome (cart add-to-cart, collaboration edit-lock, inventory hold/release, todo add/complete).

# Sequencing

```mermaid
graph LR
    1[Wire :cell_update into LV+LiveComponent] --> 2[Backpressure on Cell notify]
    1 --> 3[Cell resubscribe semantics]
    2 --> 4[Resolve Q1+Q2 design questions]
    3 --> 4
    4 --> 5[Slot-tag carries cell identity for swap detection]
    4 --> 6[Add use_cell/1 factory form]
    5 --> 7[Migrate 4 examples to use_cell]
    6 --> 7
    7 --> 8[Rename hook surface per Q2]
    8 --> 9[Delete Subscriber + legacy_* helpers + LV handlers]
    9 --> 10[Collapse Observable module; final docs+gates]
```
title: Make Cell the only subscription path; delete Observable.Subscriber
